name: knowledge-worker
description: Turning work into documents other people can act on — repo documentation, walkthrough recordings, video and meeting intake, and handoffs that survive a context reset.
$note: The kit for someone whose output is understanding rather than code — a product owner, an analyst, a technical writer. It is the one kit that assumes the least about the target repo: none of these skills needs a build, a stack, or a deploy target.
$extendsNote:
kits/README.md already said method-core is 'the floor' and that 'the others assume it is installed alongside'. That was a dependency recorded in prose and enforced by nobody — an instance bootstrapped from this kit alone got six skills and none of the method they sit on, silently. `extends` makes the sentence executable.

⚠️ AND THE FLOOR IS A LESS OBVIOUS FIT HERE THAN ANYWHERE ELSE, which is worth saying rather than smoothing over: method-core ships df-tdd-developer and dark-factory-build, and a technical writer will not run either. They are carried anyway because the floor is the estate's stated design and a kit is not the place to quietly renegotiate it. What this kit DOES need from the floor is the part nobody notices until it is missing — critical-thinking, work-autonomously, df-adversary-gate, vinculum-loop: the stance and the evidence gate. A document written by an agent that never asks 'what would prove this wrong?' is the failure mode of this whole kit.
$overlapNote: agent-notepad and handoff are also in agent-ops. That is deliberate and is NOT a 'one artifact, one home' violation: one home is about which repo OWNS the directory, and exactly one does. A kit only references a skill by name, so two kits naming it create no second copy and nothing that can drift. Kits are curated bundles; overlap between them is the normal case.
